 diaphragmatic surface is long-standing but progressed since ___.  Elective

 is approximately 4 cm beyond the GE junction.  .  There is a patchy density in

Endotracheal tube continues to have its tip approximately 4.5 cm above the
 carina.  The left internal jugular central line terminates in the proximal
 SVC.  A nasogastric tube is seen coursing below the diaphragm with the tip not
 identified.  There continues to be a diffuse interstitial abnormality with
 some superimposed patchy opacities at both bases.  There is relative sparing

 changed dating back to ___.  However, in the absence of more remote
 imaging, it is difficult to determine whether this represents pre-existing
 chronic interstitial lung disease and/or emphysematous changes or whether this

 Clinical correlation is therefore advised and comparison to outside imaging

 stable.  No pneumothorax.

 pneumomediastinum following the recent procedure.  Interval improved aeration

 decreased.  As a consequence, pre-existing areas of retrocardiac and left
 basal opacity appear slightly denser than before.  However, extent of these
 areas has not increased, which makes atelectasis more likely than pneumonia. 
 No new parenchymal opacities.  Unchanged size of the cardiac silhouette. 
 Unchanged appearance of the monitoring and support devices.

 right pleural effusion could have slightly increased.  Unchanged bilateral

Right IJ catheter tip projects over the expected region of the mid SVC.

 underlying table or bucky board.  Support lines and tubes are unchanged.

 interstitial edema.  Tip of endotracheal tube remains relatively high,

 right internal jugular vein catheter and the nasogastric tube are in stable

 left IJ catheter that extends to the mid to lower portion of the SVC.

 of superior SVC.  Bibasal consolidations and bilateral pleural effusions in

1.  ETT in standard position.
 
 2.  Multifocal pneumonia and/or heart failure, multifocal pneumonia is most

Comparison to ___.  The monitoring and support devices are stable.

Left apical lateral pneumothorax as described above.  Fractures as known.
